Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  June 6, 2024

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on June 6, 2024. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Cynthia McLemore - District
  3, Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Octavio Padilla –District 2, Commissioner Christopher
  Beck – District 4

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director
  Gilbert Gonzalez  Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Bharat Devlia  Food Services Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Anthony Harris  Recreation Supervisor

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and second by Commissioner McLemore
that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on November 2,
2023, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore, and Denmon
Noes: None

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and second by Commissioner McLemore that the
minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on March 7, 2024, be
approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore, and Denmon
Noes: None

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and second by Commissioner McLemore that the
minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on April 4, 2024, be
approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore, and Denmon
Noes: None

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Graffiti Abatement Supervisor, Gilbert Gonzalez
reported the following: The Edward Vincent Park Storm Water Improvement Project
meeting is scheduled for the third quarter of the year. Staff has identified loose pieces of
the pool deck that needed to be stabilized before the pool could open for the summer.
Staff replanted some of the parkway and triangles around the entrance to City Hall. The
graffiti crew was able to accommodate some last minute requests from Inglewood Little
League to beautify the backstop area of the big field at Rogers Park prior to the opening of
the Tournament of Champions. Park staff assisted and installed a new drinking fountain
as well. Graffiti Update – District 4 in the Darby/Dixon area, just west of Crenshaw and
north of 104th Street, was heavily tagged this month. Our graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.

REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor Anthony Harris reported the following:
Dodgers DreamTeam Baseball Summer League begins next week; 270 youth ages 9-18 in
Inglewood will begin the baseball and softball season. Arguably our most popular offering,
the Dreamteam summer season, will host game days at Edward Vincent and Darby Parks
on Thursday evenings, which showcases our Jr. Softball Division and all day on Saturdays
featuring four additional age groups. Twenty-two teams will compete over the next 8
weeks with numerous opportunities to develop their baseball/softball skills, participate in
healthy competition, have fun, and grow as young people through sports. The season will
conclude on August 24 with Championship Saturday and team banquets offering food, fun,
and awards for all involved. Come out and witness the fun! Our 90-minute youth sports
clinic series is in full swing as youngsters get an opportunity to be introduced to various
sports, develop skills, and have fun throughout the year. We recently completed a tennis
clinic for the youth a couple of weeks ago led by city partner 40 Love Foundation. A sold-
out youth soccer clinic was executed last Saturday in collaboration with partner Jose
Palomares of PCSC at Champions Field. Other sports offered through this series are
volleyball, lacrosse, and a fitness and agility clinic. These clinics allow us to introduce new
sports like volleyball and lacrosse to the community with a goal of developing enough
interest in the city to create a future league. The chance to explore new sports is essential
and we are pleased to provide these opportunities. The Parks, Recreation and Community
Services Department is gearing up for the summer! It is time to get in and get wet at the
pool located at Edward Vincent Park. The pool officially opens Saturday June 15 offering
swim lessons, family swim nights, and aqua groove for seniors, and recreational swim. We
have something for everyone whether you are trying to beat the heat, learn new strokes,
or cool off with friends. Join us at Edward Vincent Park this summer. We are excited to
announce that our Summer Day Camp programs for Rogers and Darby Parks are FULL. Our
Kiddie Camp for tots ages 3-5 at Siminski Park has a few spaces available for the 3rd and 4th
sessions. Campers will enjoy a different theme each session and participate in enrichment
programming, social recreation, arts and crafts, specialty activities, field trips, and more!

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

Join the Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department for our summer annual
“Movies in the Park” series. Our first movie will be shown at Edward Vincent Park on
Saturday, June 29, featuring the famous movie Trolls – Band Together. Arrive early and
join us for a Trolls dance party before the film begins. All movies are free and begin at dusk.
Food and refreshments will be available for purchase. Bring ten recyclable items, and you
will automatically be entered into a raffle to win prizes. You have all received a copy of
the flyer. We encourage you to grab your blankets and lawn chairs and join us for an
unforgettable evening at the cinema under the stars. For more information on our
Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports website at:
https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Supervisor, Bharat Devlia reported the
following: We are serving approximately 450 seniors per week through home-delivered
meals for homebound seniors and congregate meals at our Senior Center. Since the
beginning of May, we have started a trial breakfast and dinner program in addition to our
regular lunch program, serving three meals a day for seven days per week. Each of the
three meals provides at least one-third of the recommended daily allowances for key
nutrients such as vitamins A and C, potassium, protein, and fiber. We have received a
tremendous amount of positive feedback about this trial program, which continues
through June 30, after which we will return to providing lunches only. We continue to
provide fresh produce weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute and
started a new food kit program in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank on May
23. Seniors can register for a monthly free nutritious package that includes a selection of
fruit, juice, vegetables, milk, cheese, grains, protein, and much more. This food box is
designed to supplement the dietary intake of calcium, potassium, magnesium, fiber, and
vitamins. The next food box distribution will be at our Senior Center on Monday, June 24.
For more information, please call the Senior Center at 310-412-5338. Transportation. Our
paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors and the disabled community in
Inglewood and Hawthorne. Recently, we have been working collaboratively with the
California Integrated Travel Project to integrate the City’s I-Line Trolley service with Google
Maps, allowing seniors to find I-Line stops using the public transit icon in Google
Maps. Our new taxi program has been successful since its recent inception and we have
found it to be an improvement in reliability compared to our previous program. Senior
Center Operations. Our Senior Center continues to thrive with a plethora of activities and
special events coming up. Our highlights for June include a first-time tour at the Beckmen
YOLA on June 3 here on LaBrea Avenue, with registrations for the trip currently open. We
are also proud to announce our collaboration with the Los Angeles County Aging &
Disabilities Department to provide free tablets for our seniors. Provide context re:
downtown collection. We have 48 seniors registered for tablets so far, and our distribution
dates are June 6 and June 13. We will have a grand Father’s Day Celebration on June 14,
with special performances by our choir, a live band, poetry reading, and a gift giveaway to

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

our special fathers. On June 19, we will be have our first official Juneteenth celebration.
This will be in collaboration with Generation Connect and AARP, and our seniors can look
forward to a guest speaker, special performances, food, and a vibrantly decorated Senior
Center. The Child and Adult Care Food Program known as CACFP, will end on June 7, 2024.
The CACFP serves meals to youth 18 years old and under and operates at Crenshaw Library,
Inglewood Main Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park. The program's hours are Monday
through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 PM - 3:30 PM and snacks from 4:30 PM - 5:00
PM. We serve an average of 115 suppers and 50 snacks per week. The Summer Food
Service Program will commence on June 17, 2024. We will serve at six different locations
for youth 18 and under. The sites are Ashwood Park, Crenshaw Library, Darby Park,
Siminski Park, Rogers Park, and Edward Vincent Park. We will provide breakfast, lunch, and
snacks at different sites, and the times will vary according to the sites.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Director Thomas Uwal reported on the following: the Parks,
Recreation and Community Services Department will have two events scheduled for
Juneteenth Day. There will be a tree-planting day at Edward Vincent Park with the
Community beautifying our park and a Juneteenth event planned at the Inglewood Senior
Center with music and nationally recognized speakers educating the community about
Freedom Day. We ask our Parks and Recreation Commissioners to join us at both events
to commemorate Juneteenth. We are currently meeting with our Public Works Director
to plan Capital Improvement Projects for all our Parks in our FY 2025 budget. Our
Department is giving our priority list for the next fiscal year, and I look forward to sharing
it with our commissioners once it is finalized and approved. A budget Kick-off Meeting has
been scheduled with to discuss the development and instructions for the FY2024-25
budget. Our Department is preparing to request the necessary funds needed to operate
for the coming fiscal year.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner McLemore thanked staff for their reports
and hard work.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at 6:32 p.m.
